purpose: Primary-source verification and completion of the occupation-salary matrix. Each figure is tagged with a verification status: PRIMARY_VERIFIED (locateable on the publishing institution's own table/page), PRIMARY_SOURCE_IDENTIFIED_PENDING (official publisher/table confirmed but the exact cell was not machine-extractable here - do NOT promote), or GAP (the institution does not publish the needed granularity). Aggregator/employer figures are never recorded.
basis_convention: GROSS medians, whole occupation / occupation-class, all experience levels. Not entry-level, not degree-specific, not take-home. Metric definition and unit recorded per cell because institutions differ (monthly vs weekly vs annual; occupation vs occupation-class).

corrections.correction: CONFIRMED WRONG. Stats NZ DOES publish 'HLFS: Earnings from main wage and salary job by occupation (ANZSCO 2006)' (released 27 Aug 2025 / 5 Aug 2026). However the accessible published chart surfaces only 1-digit ANZSCO MAJOR GROUP medians (Professionals NZ$1,784/week June 2025), NOT the detailed software/civil engineer occupations. See gap.

The CBS table 85517NED 'Werknemers; uurloon en beroep' is CONFIRMED OFFICIAL (CC-BY, OData API) but was STOPPED (stopgezet) on 18-08-2026 and superseded by a successor table. The 0811 monthly figure must be re-verified against the successor table before promotion. Primary expression is gross HOURLY median by occupation.

German software developer figures from employer/survey sites are AGGREGATOR/CROWDSOURCED and are excluded. German occupation earnings must come from BA Entgeltatlas occupation-CLASS medians, which mix vocational (Fachkraft) and academic (Expert) tracks - a definition difference that must be labelled.

canada_note: Canada (Job Bank / Statistics Canada LFS) is the publishing institution and was already read at primary level in waves 1-2 (NOC 21232 software dev median CAD 48.08/hr; NOC 21211 data scientist CAD 46.15/hr; NOC 21300 civil engineer CAD 48.56/hr; ref 2023-2024, wages updated 2025-11-19). These are PRIMARY_VERIFIED against jobbank.gc.ca occupation wage reports. Some regional rows are SAE model estimates (ESTIMATE) and are excluded; only direct LFS national/provincial rows used.
conflicting_definitions: Occupation vs occupation-CLASS: US/GB report single-SOC occupations; DE reports occupation-CLASS (Berufsgattung) medians mixing experience tracks; AU/NL report 4-digit/an occupation-class medians. All are occupation-level (rule #4 satisfied) but the granularity differs and must be labelled so a class figure is not read as one role.

Period unit: DE = monthly; CA/AU/NZ = weekly (NZ group) or hourly; US/GB/NL(secondary) = annual or hourly. Annualisation multiplies by assumed hours, which is a derivation and must be flagged, not silently done.
Basis: all gross/wage medians; none net. NZ/AU 'before tax'. No cell supports a take-home figure.

German vocational vs academic: BA data covers social-insurance employees (excludes self-employed/civil servants and pay above the Beitragsbemessungsgrenze), and splits Fachkraft vs Expert tracks - a CS Master's graduate maps to the Expert track whose exact median was not extracted.
